root_cause.summary: Ubuntu 24.04 (noble) arm64 heaptrack (1.5.0+dfsg1-2build2) + nongnu libunwind8 (1.6.2-3build1) emits zero stack frames (trace index 0) for all allocations on aarch64
mechanism: On Ubuntu 24.04 arm64, /usr/lib/heaptrack/libheaptrack_preload.so is compiled with -mbranch-protection=standard (paciasp/autiasp and DWARF .cfi_negate_ra_state / DW_CFA_AARCH64_negate_ra_state 0x2d).
nongnu libunwind 1.6.2 on arm64 does not support DW_CFA_AARCH64_negate_ra_state in its DWARF CFI evaluator and aborts unwinding after at most 2 internal frames.
In heaptrack_malloc (offset 0x6530..0x6574 in libheaptrack_preload.so), heaptrack computes frame_count = max(unw_backtrace(buf, 64), 2) - 2 to strip Trace::unwind and heaptrack_malloc.
Because unw_backtrace returns <= 2 when called from a PAC-enabled frame, frame_count is 0 for every allocation (+ <size> 0 <addr>), even on /bin/ls.
Consequently allocations.gz contains zero i/t stack records (all 650 allocations report 0x0 in ??), and measure-operation.py fails with ValueError: Missing unique operation markers.
GitHub Actions (.github/workflows/workspace.yml) runs on ubuntu-24.04 x86_64 where ARM64 PAC is absent and where measure-operation.py stack/size rules were calibrated.
